title: Pointwise convergence of consecutive triple ergodic averages under mixing
exact_target: For every invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation T and bounded measurable f,g,h, do $(1/N)sum_{n=1}^N$ $f(T^n$ $x)g(T^{2n}x)h(T^{3n}x)$ converge almost everywhere to (integral f)(integral g)(integral h)?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
For every invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation T and bounded measurable f,g,h, do $(1/N)sum_{n=1}^N$ $f(T^n$ $x)g(T^{2n}x)h(T^{3n}x)$ converge almost everywhere to (integral f)(integral g)(integral h)?

\subsection{Short English statement}
For every invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation T and bounded measurable f,g,h, do $(1/N)sum_{n=1}^N$ $f(T^n$ $x)g(T^{2n}x)h(T^{3n}x)$ converge almost everywhere to (integral f)(integral g)(integral h)?
